tracks.useful_outcome: Short, visible results that build directly on the accepted bound: one session each.

tasks.question: Redo the zero-pairing proof (research/zero-pairing/PROOF.md) for general beta, and give an explicit-witness-bound claim at Xu-Sang's theta = 8748867/10000000: the first explicit deterministic Miller-Rabin with running-time exponent below 10 (about 9.9928).
starting_points: research/zero-pairing/PROOF.md (Lemma 0', steps (b)-(f); 'Sanity check' gives the general-beta forms)
methods: Restate Lemma 0' with beta/(1-beta) in place of 7 and c2 >= 1/(2 sqrt(beta(1-beta))); redo (b)-(f) with K = 1/(1-beta), which is not an integer, so bound every irrational power by an exact rational in the safe direction; write a new constants.py and a candidates/*.json claim. A float probe suggests C about 0.528 and log10 W(2^1024) about 20.57.

tasks.question: Implement the accepted deterministic test: an odd n is prime iff no prime p <= max(41, (0.529 ln n)^8) is a strong witness, with the bound computed rigorously (never rounded down).
methods: Write impl/deterministic_mr.py (stdlib only): the first 13 primes below psi_13, else a prime sieve to the bound; a rigorous integer upper bound for (0.529 ln n)^8 using check.ln_bounds; tests against is_prime_trial for n < 10^6 and against the psi table; a short README with the base count at 64, 128 and 1024 bits.
tasks.acceptance_gate: A PR adding impl/ and tests under tests/, all passing; the bound computation shown never to round down.

first_step.scope: Positive control: the existing tests pass.

tasks.bottleneck_link: Turns the theorem into something a donor can run. Below psi_13 it is fast; above, it is honest about being impractical.

tasks.question: Under H(7/8), give an explicit bound for the least prime l not dividing q and not in a proper subgroup H of (Z/qZ)* (LLS Theorem 1.1), and for the least quadratic non-residue mod a prime q (LLS Corollary 1.1).
starting_points: research/zero-pairing/PROOF.md (step (a) onwards: the Miller-Rabin case is H = the liar subgroup)
LLS arXiv:1309.3595, Theorem 1.1, Corollary 1.1 and Section 3
methods: Part 2 of LLS Theorem 1.1 (q has no prime factor below X) is the zero-pairing argument almost verbatim; handle general q via LLS Lemma 3.1 and (3.2). For prime q, choose y_min so the bound applies above a q0 small enough to settle q < q0 by direct computation.

tasks.question: Under H(7/8), give an explicit bound for the least prime in a coset aH of a subgroup H of (Z/qZ)* (LLS Theorem 1.4), and so for the least prime P(a, q) in an arithmetic progression (LLS Corollary 1.2).
starting_points: LLS arXiv:1309.3595, Theorem 1.4, Corollary 1.2 and Section 4
methods: Follow LLS Section 4 (orthogonality over the h characters trivial on H), replacing each GRH zero-sum estimate with Lemma 0'; track the extra (h - 1) factor; the expected shape is P(a, q) <= (c phi(q) log q)^8.

tasks.question: What explicit upper and lower bounds for |L(1, chi)|, and hence for class numbers h(-q), follow from H(7/8)? (LLS Theorem 1.5 and Corollary 1.3 do this under GRH with log log q.)
starting_points: LLS arXiv:1309.3595, Theorem 1.5, Corollary 1.3 and Section 5
methods: Redo LLS Section 5 with zeros allowed up to Re s = 7/8. Expect much weaker bounds than GRH's log log q: likely a power of log q. First work out the right shape, then make it explicit.

tasks.question: What are the best explicit bounds, valid for every conductor q <= n, on sum over nontrivial zeros rho of L(s, chi) of |w-hat(rho)| for a fixed smooth weight w, in the form a ln q + b?
starting_points: Trudgian, An improved upper bound for the error in the zero-counting formulae for Dirichlet L-functions and Dedekind zeta-functions, Math. Comp. 84 (2015)
Bennett, Martin, O'Bryant, Rechnitzer, Explicit bounds for primes in arithmetic progressions, Illinois J. Math. 62 (2018)
McCurley, Explicit estimates for the error term in the prime number theorem for arithmetic progressions, Math. Comp. 42 (1984)
methods: Literature extraction: state each explicit zero-counting theorem exactly, with hypotheses and constants, and derive the a ln q + b bound by partial summation for one or two standard weights.
